subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Suppose A and B are independent events with P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.7. Compute (i) P(A ∩ B) (ii) P(A ∪ B) (iii) P(B|A) (iv) P(Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the four quantities for independent events with P(A) = 0.6 and P(B) = 0.7 — the rule each part uses and the number.
insider_note: Part (iii) is a one-line answer: for independent events P(B|A) is just P(B). Students lose that mark by computing P(A ∩ B)/P(A) — which gives the same 0.7, but slowly.

steps.label: A and B are independent
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. Write the given values and the word "independent" — it is the reason behind parts (i), (iii) and (iv).

recall.must_convey: That A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.6 and P(B) = 0.7.
accept: A and B are independent with P A point six and P B point seven
the events are independent, point six and point seven
independent events, P of A is 0.6 and P of B is 0.7
A B independent, P A 0.6, P B 0.7 ani given

steps.why: Independence is what turns P(A ∩ B) into a product; without that word none of the four parts can start.
common_mistakes: Not writing "independent" and then using the product rule with no reason.

steps.label: (i) P(A ∩ B)

recall.must_convey: That for independent events P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B) = 0.6 × 0.7 = 0.42.
accept: P of A intersection B is P A times P B which is point four two
independent so multiply point six by point seven to get 0.42
the intersection is the product 0.42
independent kabatti P A into P B, 0.42

steps.why: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B) is the definition of independence; it is the only formula for the intersection when no overlap is given.

steps.label: (ii) P(A ∪ B)

lines.text: (ii) P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

accept: P of A union B is P A plus P B minus P A intersection B which is point eight eight
addition theorem 0.6 plus 0.7 minus 0.42 equals 0.88
the union is one point three minus point four two
addition theorem tho 0.6 plus 0.7 minus 0.42 ante 0.88

steps.why: The union counts the overlap twice, so the intersection just found is subtracted once.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as 1.3, which is more than 1 and cannot be a probability.
Subtracting P(A)·P(B) written as 0.42 but then adding it.

steps.label: (iii) P(B|A)
steps.margin_note: For independent events the condition changes nothing: P(B|A) = P(B) = 0.7.

recall.must_convey: That for independent events P(B|A) = P(B) = 0.7.
accept: P of B given A equals P of B which is point seven because they are independent
independent so the conditional probability is just P B, 0.7
B given A is point seven
independent kabatti P B given A ante P B, 0.7

steps.why: Independence means knowing A happened does not change the chance of B. P(B|A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A) = 0.42/0.6 = 0.7 confirms it.

steps.label: (iv) P(Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ)
steps.margin_note: Aᶜ and Bᶜ are also independent, so multiply the complements: 0.4 × 0.3 = 0.12.

lines.text: (iv) Aᶜ, Bᶜ are also independent, so

recall.must_convey: That the complements are independent too, so P(Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ) = (1 − 0.6)(1 − 0.7) = 0.4 × 0.3 = 0.12.
accept: the complements are independent so P of A complement and B complement is point four times point three which is point one two
one minus point six times one minus point seven equals 0.12
neither A nor B is 0.4 into 0.3
complements kuda independent, 0.4 into 0.3 ante 0.12

steps.why: Aᶜ ∩ Bᶜ is "neither A nor B", the complement of A ∪ B: 1 − 0.88 = 0.12, the same number — a check that both routes agree.
common_mistakes: Using 0.6 and 0.7 instead of their complements.
